A Chinese Buddhist monk of the Tang era who travelled by sea to India and back, and left the best early account of Srivijaya, the Buddhist kingdom of Sumatra.

Yijing sailed from Guangzhou in 671 on a Persian ship. He stopped in Srivijaya for six months to learn Sanskrit grammar, then went on to India, where he studied for about ten years at the great monastery of Nalanda. On the way home he stayed in Srivijaya again for several years, copying and translating texts. He advised other Chinese pilgrims to study there first, since its monks followed the same rules as in India.

He returned to Luoyang in 695 and was welcomed by Empress Wu Zetian. He spent his last years translating dozens of Buddhist texts. His two books, a record of Buddhist practice in India and the islands and a set of lives of monks who went west, are key sources on the sea route between China and India. He followed the overland pilgrims Faxian and Xuanzang. See also Yijing at Srivijaya.
sum: A Chinese Buddhist monk of the Tang era who travelled by sea to India and back, and left the best early account of Srivijaya, the Buddhist kingdom of Sumatra.
